original_question: Can we find f ∈ Diff ∞ 0 (Σg ) such that scl(f ) = 0 but f is not a commutator?
target_in_paper: Section 7.1, Question 7.2: "Can we find f ∈ Diff_0^∞(Σ_g) such that scl(f) = 0 but f is not a commutator? What about Homeo_0(Σ_g)?"
correct_elements: Your draft captures the main target almost exactly: it identifies the smooth identity-component surface diffeomorphism group Diff_0^∞(Σ_g), asks for an element f with vanishing stable commutator length, and asks that f fail to be a single commutator. This is precisely the first half of Question 7.2.
missing_details: The paper explicitly places the question on a surface Σ_g of genus g ≥ 1.
The notation Diff_0^∞(Σ_g) uses the identity component (the subscript 0), and the nearby paper notation Homeo_0(Σ_g) uses the same convention.
The preceding paragraph defines stable commutator length: scl(f) = lim_{n→∞} cl(f^n)/n, where cl is the word length with respect to the set of commutators.
The official formulation also asks the analogous question for Homeo_0(Σ_g); your draft only includes the Diff_0^∞(Σ_g) half.
The sentence immediately after Question 7.2 explains the intended motivation: to detect that an element is not a commutator without relying on quasimorphisms.
Later on the same page, the paper notes that Question 7.2 has already been answered negatively by Theorem 4.1 of Matsumoto [Mat87], so this is not presented there as a still-open problem.
refined_question: Let Σ_g be a surface of genus g ≥ 1. Does there exist an element f in the identity component Diff_0^∞(Σ_g) of the C^∞ diffeomorphism group such that its stable commutator length scl(f), defined by scl(f) = lim_{n→∞} cl(f^n)/n where cl is commutator length, is zero, but f is not a single commutator [a,b] = aba^{-1}b^{-1}? Likewise, does such an example exist in Homeo_0(Σ_g)?
justification: The draft is aimed directly at Section 7.1, Question 7.2. The paper first defines stable word length and stable commutator length in the paragraph immediately preceding the question, then states Question 7.2 for Diff_0^∞(Σ_g), with Σ_g a surface of genus g ≥ 1, and immediately appends the parallel Homeo_0(Σ_g) version. The next sentence explains that the point is to develop methods for proving an element is not a commutator without using quasimorphisms. Finally, the paper itself records, on the same page, that this question has a negative answer by Matsumoto’s Theorem 4.1. So your draft is very close, but it omits the genus restriction, the definition of scl, the official Homeo_0(Σ_g) companion question, and the paper’s note that the question is already negatively resolved.
